segments.en:
that was revealed in Tiberias seventy years ago,

and it has great value in the eyes of those who reveal it, the Breslov Hasidim.

We are hosting three people here: Aharon Fetz, Sharon Taltsur, and Rebbe Yisrael Dov Odesser.

Let us hear a little from you, Sharon: what is this special story with this petek? How was it revealed? Under what circumstances?] [Sixty-three years ago, to be more precise, this petek was found by Rabbi Odesser,

who, five days before the petek was found, failed in the fast of the seventeenth of Tammuz.

And for five days as a result he fell into depression, because he had already been accustomed to fasting from the age of six, Mondays and Thursdays, and here this was a public fast, a public fast which according to the Shulchan Aruch must be observed, and he failed in it.

So for five days he was depressed, until it entered his mind that perhaps the remedy,

the remedy, would be in his bookcase, which was locked,

because Breslov books were then forbidden to be touched by the other Hasidim.

He went in and opened the cabinet and took a book, opened it, and found the petek inside.

And in the petek it is written:

“It was very difficult for me to descend to you, my precious student, to tell you that I derived great pleasure from your service,

and about you I said: ‘My little fire will burn until the Messiah comes.’

Be strong and courageous in your service. Na Nach Nachma Nachman of Uman.”

And after this story there is a secret, and it is:

“Full and heaped from line to line (P.Tz.P.Tz.Y.H.).”

This is a sign that the petek descended from Heaven and was not merely found by chance: “The seventeenth of Tammuz will be a sign; they will say that you are not fasting.”

He did not reveal to anyone that he had failed in the fast of the seventeenth of Tammuz,

to no one except the Holy One, blessed be He. He failed; he did not want to]

[And how is that written in the petek?]

[And this is written in the petek, that this petek descended..]
